metadata.description: Synthetic post-impact incident reports for the triage demo (not real events).

incidents.title: Dialysis patients stranded – medical evacuation needed
incidents.description: Three dialysis patients and one pregnant woman in labour cannot reach Hospital O'Horán; road to Kinchil flooded.

incidents.title: Coastal highway Progreso–Telchac blocked by debris and sand
incidents.description: Km 12–18 of the coastal road buried under sand and fallen poles; isolates Chicxulub Puerto and Uaymitún.

incidents.title: Shelter at 96% capacity – Escuela secundaria (Sisal)
incidents.description: Shelter receiving evacuees from coastal colonias; water and bedding running low, 40 more families arriving.

incidents.title: Power substation flooded – Valladolid east
incidents.description: Substation flooded with 0.6 m of water; outage affects General Hospital backup feed and water pumping station.

incidents.title: Families on rooftops – storm surge in fishing neighbourhood
incidents.description: Approx. 25 people including children on rooftops near the estuary; water level still rising.

incidents.title: Urban flooding in underpass – vehicles trapped
incidents.description: Periférico underpass flooded (1.2 m); two vehicles trapped, drivers evacuated by bystanders.

incidents.title: Elderly residents without medication – Maya-speaking comisaría
incidents.description: Comisaría reports 15 elderly residents (Maya-speaking only) without insulin/hypertension medication; road partially open.

incidents.title: Communication tower down – El Cuyo isolated
incidents.description: Only cell tower collapsed; no news from approx. 1,800 residents since 05:00. Status unknown.

incidents.title: Fallen trees on rural road – Tizimín ranch area
incidents.description: Several trees across secondary road to ejidos; no injuries reported, alternative route available.

incidents.title: Shelter generator failure – Mérida sports complex
incidents.description: Backup generator failed at shelter hosting 1,100 people; refrigerated medicines at risk within 4 h.
